messages.content: What wheather is now in Moscow, in celsius?

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have real‑time data access. I can’t look up the current temperature in Moscow right now. If you’d like, I can show you how to use a weather API (like OpenWeatherMap) to get that information programmatically.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current weather in Moscow. We need to provide the current temperature in Celsius. We don't have direct access to real-time data. We can either approximate or say we can't fetch real-time data. According to policy, we should not fabricate. We can say we don't have real-time data. We can suggest using a weather API. So we respond that we cannot fetch real-time data.
